info.title: MoneyBadger Wallet QR Scanner API
info.description:
# MoneyBadger Wallet QR Scanner API
This API enables a partner wallet to scan QR codes and receive a payment request. It provides several endpoints: one to retrieve the API swagger specification, another to report scanned QR codes, and a third to query the status of a payment request.

# Example Usage
The following example demonstrates how to obtain a PaymentRequest containing a lightning invoice using the API:

```bash
    SCAN_ID=$(uuidgen) # Generates a unique scan identifier
    USER_ID=$(uuidgen) # Generates a unique user identifier
    DEVICE_ID=$(uuidgen) # Generates a unique device identifier
    API_KEY="API KEY HERE" # Replace with your actual API key
    QR_DATA=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -D - 'https://staging.circuit.cryptoconvert.co.za/test/qr.png?amountCents=100&completion=confirm' | grep x-mpm-code | sed 's/x-mpm-code: //' | tr -d '\r') # Fetches QR data
    curl -X POST "https://api.staging.cryptoqr.net/scanner/v1/scan" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
    -d '{
        "scan_id": "'"$SCAN_ID"'",
        "time": "'"$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")"'",
        "device_id": "'"$DEVICE_ID"'",
        "user_id": "'"$USER_ID"'",
        "scan_data": "'"$QR_DATA"'",
        "allowed_payment_methods": ["lightning"],
        "payment_currencies": ["BTC"]
    }' | jq .
```

# Expected Workflow

1. The wallet app scans the QR code.
2. The wallet app sends the entire QR code payload to the /scan endpoint.
3. The scan endpoint returns a payment request, which includes all necessary information for the wallet to complete the payment, e.g. a Lightning invoice.
4. The wallet authorizes the payment, for example by making a Lightning invoice payment.
5. The Point of Sale (POS) system will either CONFIRM or CANCEL the payment:
  a. If CONFIRM, the wallet must finalize the transaction.
  b. If CANCEL, the wallet must cancel the transaction and return funds to the user.

# Testing the API
To test the API, you can use the following URL to obtain a QR code that can be scanned:
https://staging.circuit.cryptoconvert.co.za/test/qr.png?amountCents=100&completion=confirm

- The `amountCents` parameter allows you to set the amount for the payment request.
- The `completion` parameter simulates the final advice behavior by the POS:
  - Setting it to `confirm` will immediately confirm the payment request upon payment.
  - Setting it to `cancel` will immediately cancel the payment request upon payment.

A similar QR code can be used to test the production API by changing the host in the URL to `api.cryptoqr.net`, for example:
https://api.cryptoqr.net/test/qr.png?amountCents=100&completion=confirm

For automation purposes, the test QR code includes a header `x-mpm-code` which contains the scan data.

# Errors
Error responses are returned in cases of invalid input or other errors. The expected error codes include:
  - UNKNOWN_CODE: The scanned code was not recognized.
  - SMART_SHOPPER_SCANNED: The scanned code was a smart shopper code. Please ask the cashier to allow you to "Pay with a QR code."
  - AMOUNT_TOO_HIGH: The transaction amount exceeded the allowed limit.
  - LIGHTNING_INVOICE_SCANNED: The transaction was a Lightning invoice rather than a recognized QR code.


# Production Access
To access the production API, use the `api.cryptoqr.net` host. Production API keys are issued by MoneyBadger after the partner application has been reviewed and thoroughly tested in the staging environment.

# Staging Access
To access the staging API, use the `api.staging.cryptoqr.net` host. Staging API keys are provided by MoneyBadger once the partner has signed the necessary agreements and completed the onboarding process.

get.summary: Get QR code information about a scanned QR code, this information can be used to tailor wallet UI and enhance user experience

post.summary: reports that a QR code has been scanned by the partner app, obtain payment instructions specific to the wallet

get.summary: gets the latest payment request status

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Payment request ID provided during /scan POST request (e.g. paymentRequestID-6c54-4b01-90e6-d701748f0851)

200.description: payment request status has been successfully retrieved

404.description: payment request ID was not found

scan_id.description: a unique ID for the scan, preferably a UUID

transaction_id.description: (Optional) A unique ID for the transaction, preferably a UUID. This ID may be specified by the API consumer when calling the /scan endpoint. This ID must be the reference that the Value Store uses to identify the transaction. if provided, the transaction_id will used to query payment status on the value store.

time.description: The date and time of the message as recorded by the sender in ISO8601 format

device_id.description: the device ID of the device that scanned the QR code, preferably a UUID

user_id.description: the user ID of the user that scanned the QR code, preferably a UUID

payment_currencies.description: The currencies of the payment request that the receiver is able to to use for payment. optional, defaults to the default of the payment method

payment_reference.description: The customer-supplied reference for the payment request

denomination.description: The denomination of the currency (e.g. cents, sats)

amount.description: The payment amount in the specified denomination

Error.description:
Error response in case of invalid input or other errors
Expected error codes:
- UNKNOWN_CODE - the scanned code was not recognised
- SMART_SHOPPER_SCANNED - the scanned code was a smart shopper code, please ask the cashier to allow you to "Pay with a QR code"
- AMOUNT_TOO_HIGH - the transaction amount was too high
- LIGHTNING_INVOICE_SCANNED - the transaction was a Lightning invoice rather than a known QR code

id.description: A unique ID that we assign to the payment request.

transaction_id.description: (Optional) The transaction ID that was specified by the API consumer on the /scan endpoint.

created_at.description: ISO8601 timestamp at which the payment request was created

amount_cents.description: The amount of the payment request in the currency base unit (e.g. cents or sats)

currency.description: The currency of the payment request that the receiver expects to receive

status.description: The current status of the payment request

payment_methods.description: list of payment method types with payment instruction data the client can use to complete payment

expiry_time.description: ISO8601 timestamp at which the payment request will expire

notification_url.description: A URL that must be called whenever the status of this payment request changes (paid, cancelled, etc) The notification_url must be called with a POST request with a JSON body. The details of the JSON body may be determined by the implementer, but MUST include a transaction_id The transaction_id must be the same as the transaction_id provided in the /scan request that we can use to query the status on the Value Store.

merchant_info.description: Additional merchant information, structure depends on specific merchant.

refund_info.description: Refund information related to this payment request

QrCodeInfo.description:
Information about the QR code to be displayed to the user or used to enhance wallet UI/UX. Use as follows:
  - amountMin > 0 and amountMin == amountMax: The QR code is for a fixed amount payment, the wallet can immediately proceed to request payment instruction (scanQr)
  - amountMin > 0 and amountMin != amountMax: The QR code is for a range payment, e.g a bill with a tip. If amountMax is 0, the wallet should allow any amount greater than amountMin.
  - amountMin == 0 and amountMax == 0: The QR code is for an unspecified payment amount, the wallet should request that the user enter an amount.
  - orderReferenceRequired == true: The QR code is for a payment that requires an order reference. The wallet should request that the user enter an order reference.

amountMin.description: Minimum amount in cents, 0 for no minimum amount

amountMax.description: Maximum amount in cents, 0 for no maximum amount

amountDefault.description: Default amount in cents, 0 for no default amount. Show this as the default value in the amount input field.

orderReferenceRequired.description: Whether an order reference is required. The order reference is a user-entered string that can be by the merchant to track the payment.

orderReferenceDefault.description: Default order reference, if orderReferenceRequired is true. Show this as the default value in the order reference input field.

tipEnabled.description: Whether the currrent payment supports tipping. Wallet should allow a tip to be set and added to the payment amount.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the QR code was created (if available)

RefundInfo.description: A summary of refunds for a payment request.

status.description: The overall refund status for the payment.

refunds.description: A list of individual refund transactions.

id.description: ID is the id of the refund

invoice_id.description: Invoice ID is the id of the invoice to refund

status.description: Status is the status of the refund
